description:
North-star capstone for OUTRAM PARK: drive an end-to-end reactor multiphysics
simulation FROM a Final Safety Analysis Report (FSAR)-level plant description,
including radiological source-term calculations.

Vision: given an FSAR-level input (geometry, materials, core loading, operating
envelope, design-basis accident/transient scenarios), produce:
  1. Nuclear data + multigroup cross sections (njoy-outram-park-fork).
  2. Geometry/mesh + Monte Carlo reference (outram-mc-libs / OpenMC-like).
  3. Coupled multiphysics: deterministic neutronics (GeN-Foam diffusion/SP3/SN) +
     thermal-hydraulics + thermo-mechanics + point kinetics (teh-o-prke), over the
     transient/accident scenarios.
  4. Source-term calculations: fission-product inventory + depletion/transmutation
     (outram-mc-libs depletion), release fractions + transport (boon-lay /
     TRISO-ATOPS Eulerian + Lagrangian), coolant activity / plate-out, and the
     released radionuclide source term.
  5. V&V against published FSAR / benchmark transients.

Ties together essentially the whole suite (njoy -> openmc -> genfoam -> source
terms), with nee_soon as the coupling/orchestration layer and, later, KOVAN to
extract FSAR/thesis inputs into structured form. Long-term / aspirational --
matures as each pillar matures; depends on op-cjw (nuclear data), op-u6s (MC),
op-p6p (GeN-Foam multiphysics), op-b4a (source terms/TRISO release), op-fr2
(nee_soon coupling).

INTENDED-USE (mandatory, RESPONSIBLE_USE.md): OUTRAM PARK is for education,
research, capability-building, and V&V ONLY. This epic is NOT for real FSAR
preparation, licensing, safety-critical decision-making, or operational/emergency
use, and must not be framed as authoritative for any of those.
title: FSAR-to-multiphysics simulation with source-term calculations (capstone vision)

acceptance_criteria: Written feasibility assessment committed (FV-vs-FEM mapping, GeN-Foam overlap, recommended path + effort estimate); no large implementation until the recommendation is accepted.
description: Investigate translating Moltres (MOOSE-based, MSRE-VALIDATED MSR multiphysics: group neutron diffusion + drift-flux delayed-neutron precursors + salt TH) into an OpenFOAM-style finite-volume formulation on outram-foam, rather than porting MOOSE (which is finite-element + PETSc + MPI and is banned by the workspace no-FFI/no-PETSc/no-MPI rule). FEASIBILITY IS UNCERTAIN and this bead is a SPIKE first, not a commitment. Key finding to weigh in design: GeN-Foam (GPL-3, already the on-hold OpenFOAM port parked in outram-foam-appbuilder-lib) ALREADY implements circulating-fuel neutronics + delayed-neutron precursor drift + TH in a finite-volume OpenFOAM setting — so reviving/extending the GeN-Foam port may be the better vehicle, with Moltres used as the reference formulation + validation yardstick (it is validated against MSRE). Deliverable of this bead: a written feasibility assessment (FV vs FEM mapping of the drift-flux precursor + group-diffusion equations; overlap with GeN-Foam; recommended path) BEFORE any large implementation. LICENSE: Moltres LGPL/GPL — reference use; verify before reusing any code. Untrusted AI-assisted draft pending human V&V.
design: Spike: map Moltres's group-diffusion + circulating-precursor + salt-TH equation set onto outram-foam FV operators; compare against GeN-Foam's existing circulating-fuel implementation; recommend (a) extend GeN-Foam port vs (b) fresh Moltres-formulation port. Output = assessment doc + recommendation, not production code.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: License due-diligence (2026-08-04): Moltres = arfc/moltres (UIUC ARFC), LGPL -> GPLv3-COMPATIBLE (LGPL code may be used in a GPL-3 work). OK as reference AND for code reuse if desired. Confirmed MOOSE-based finite-element (PETSc) -> a direct MOOSE port is banned (no-FFI/PETSc/MPI rule); this bead stays a feasibility spike mapping Moltres's validated MSR formulation onto outram-foam FV / the existing GeN-Foam port.

title: Feasibility + spike: translate Moltres physics into an OpenFOAM (outram-foam) formulation, not MOOSE

description:
kovan lit import only accepts PDFs. A great deal of open-access literature is HTML-first, so those sources cannot enter the archive at all today.

TRIGGERING CASE, 2026-08-12: https://file.scirp.org/Html/4-1090017_21248.htm — 'Gearbox Scheme in High Temperature Reactor Helium Gas Turbine System', Tsinghua INET, 2012. A legitimate HTR-10 source (phase-two helium gas-turbine cycle) that had to be read with curl and a regex because kovan could not take it. The workspace CLAUDE.md mandates kovan for document management, so a format it cannot read is a hole in the mandated workflow, not a minor inconvenience.

WHAT IS WANTED: kovan lit import accepting an HTML file or a URL, producing the same KovanDocument + markdown pair it produces for a PDF, so HTML sources land in the archive with their metadata and provenance intact rather than as loose scraped text.

DESIGN NOTES:

  - The crate already depends on pulldown-cmark for the Markdown side. HTML ->
    Markdown needs an HTML parser; prefer a pure-Rust one that does not break
    the Android build (see the workspace Android/Termux rule) and does not drag
    in a C dependency.
  - Boilerplate stripping is the real work, not tag removal. A publisher page is
    mostly navigation, journal chrome, sidebars and script. The triggering case
    was 54 kB of HTML for a few kB of article. Extracting the ARTICLE and
    discarding the furniture is what makes the result citable rather than noise.
  - Metadata is usually better in HTML than in PDF: look for citation_title,
    citation_author, citation_doi, citation_date meta tags (most publishers emit
    them), plus JSON-LD. That could give kovan cleaner titles and DOIs than its
    PDF path currently extracts — note the PDF path produced 'PII: S0029-5493(02)00182-6'
    as a title for one of today's papers, which is the file's PII, not its title.
  - If a URL is accepted directly, record the retrieval URL and date in the
    KovanDocument. Provenance for a web source is weaker than for a PDF and the
    document should say when it was fetched.

WATCH THE DATA POLICY: fetching a URL makes it easy to pull in material whose
licence has not been checked. HTML ingestion should NOT imply the result is
committable — the open/proprietary split still applies, and a publisher's HTML
is no more redistributable than its PDF.

Related: op-zo7a (kovan lit import loses its output files when piped).
title: kovan lit: ingest HTML sources, not just PDF

description: One of the picked items + a roadmap MC-coupling child. Extend to_mc_geometry beyond fitted primitives/convex: emit the faceted-solid route (a general CsgSurface::Plane per triangle, DAGMC-style) so ANY closed mesh exports to outram-mc-libs CSG, feeding the Monte Carlo neutronics side of the coupled sims. Currently returns ExportError::NotImplemented for a general plane. Depends on mc-export feature (present). V&V: a non-convex L-prism exports to an MC Geometry whose inside-test matches the mesh (interior point inside, notch point outside).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: BLOCKED on outram-mc-libs (2026-07-24 finding): SurfaceKind has only XPlane/YPlane/ZPlane/Sphere/ZCylinder — NO general Plane{a,b,c,d}, no faceted/mesh volume. to_mc_geometry therefore cannot emit a general (non-axis-aligned) plane; even a ROTATED CONVEX mesh is blocked, not just non-convex. Blender side is already ready: export::to_csg_primitive emits general CsgSurface::Plane for the convex-faceted path, and export::to_faceted_solid gives the DAGMC-style non-convex boundary (triangles + winding inside-test). PREREQUISITE (in outram-mc-libs, owned by the outram-mc session): (1) add SurfaceKind::Plane{a,b,c,d} (evaluate=a*x+b*y+c*z-d, ray distance, half-space sense) -> unlocks convex-faceted meshes; (2) a faceted-volume / DAGMC surface-tracking cell for TRUE non-convex. Do NOT edit outram-mc-libs from the blender branch without coordination (merge-conflict risk with the parallel outram-mc session). Awaiting maintainer decision on ownership.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: PARTIAL (commit a942f81): the CONVEX-faceted MC export path is now UNBLOCKED — outram-mc-libs has a general Plane{a,b,c,d} surface (the old NotImplemented gate was stale), so to_mc_geometry now maps CsgSurface::Plane -> SurfaceKind::Plane and any convex polyhedron exports (one half-space/face). STILL OPEN for this bead: genuinely NON-convex meshes (faceted-solid/DAGMC) still need a real outram-mc-libs faceted-solid dependency; to_faceted_solid produces only the local mirror. So op-hzs.36 (non-convex) remains, but convex-faceted is done.

title: outram-blender: mc-export for non-convex meshes (faceted-solid/DAGMC -> outram-mc CSG)

description:
BLOCKED 2026-08-12 by op-289n. See that bead for the reproductions.

Three designs were attempted, in the order the maintainer directed:
1. Hand-rolled implicit 3-stream matrix + Picard on the IF97 (p,h) nonlinearity, solved with outram-foam-basic-lib's dense LU SquareMatrix. WORKED end to end (three zones resolved, metal time constant real, energy balance closed to round-off) but was superseded and has been DELETED per explicit instruction.
2. Direct use of outram-foam-basic-lib fvm:: operators. Not built: FvMatrix is a single-field LDU matrix, so a monolithic 3-field coupled system is not expressible without either abusing the mesh topology (3N cells with synthetic film faces, writable via the public ldu.upper/lower/diag) or a partitioned outer iteration. Superseded before implementation.
3. Composition of OPCPFluidArray (helium) <-> SolidColumn (tube metal) <-> TampinesSteamArray (water/steam) via lateral_link_new_temperature_vector_avg_conductance. BUILT AND COMPILING, but BLOCKED: TampinesSteamArray ignores its inlet enthalpy boundary condition (op-289n), so the cold stream can never be given a feedwater inlet, has no axial temperature profile, and the exchanger cannot be driven.

VERIFIED WORKING in design 3 before the blocker: OPCPFluidArray advects its inlet enthalpy correctly; SolidColumn couples and advances; the lateral-conductance formulation gives the no-cross property structurally (q_i = UA_i*(T_up_i - T_down_i) at local temperatures, sign-correct by construction, nothing clamped); SolidMaterial::SteelSS304L supplies real density and cp so the metal mass is derived from geometry rather than invented; cost is ~0.35 ms per array step, so three 8-cell arrays at a few substeps per 0.05 s plant step is affordable.

TREE STATE: reverted to HEAD. examples/htgr_sim_v1 is unchanged and the suite is green (267 lib / 19 fhr_sim_v2 / 31 htgr_sim_v1 / 15 widget_studio, 0 failed). The ORIGINAL DEFECT IS THEREFORE STILL PRESENT: primary_loop.rs computes duty as eps*C*(T_helium - T_saturation) against an isothermal saturation sink, which over-predicts duty because the superheater driving difference never collapses. That is model error, not a timestep artefact.

NEEDS A MAINTAINER DECISION: fixing op-289n means editing tampines-steam-tables, which is outside the scope granted for this task (examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/ only) and is a published crate.

=== UPDATE 2026-08-12: DELIVERED. ===
Design 3 (OPCPFluidArray <-> SolidColumn <-> TampinesSteamArray via lateral_link_new_temperature_vector_avg_conductance) is BUILT, WIRED INTO THE PLANT AND TESTED, in examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/steam_generator.rs. The op-289n blocker is fixed and the inlet enthalpy BC works.

MEASURED AT THE DESIGN POINT (2026-08-12):
- Steam outlet 441.25 degC against the published 440 degC (+1.25 K), in the coupled plant with the feedwater controller in the loop. The maintainer-visible 'steam far too hot' symptom is gone.
- Hot-end driving temperature difference 263.80 K, against 470.4 K for the isothermal-saturation-sink model it replaces -- the old model over-predicted it by 78%.
- Zero node-by-node temperature cross at every step of every run (worst 0.000000 K), structurally rather than by clamping.
- max_absorbable_duty no longer binds: peak Q_offered/Q_max 0.8807 in normal operation, 0.9088 including start-up.
- Tube metal 3184.3 kg DERIVED from geometry via SolidMaterial::SteelSS304L (8030 kg/m3), C = 1.6366e6 J/K, tau = C/UA = 38.42 s. A 100 K duty step moves the steam outlet 0.0005% in the first 0.05 s.
- Energy balance closes to +0.34% (converged; it is an explicit Lie-split coupling, so O(dt) -- 1.72% at a 0.025 s substep, 0.35% at 0.00625 s).
- Helium terminals sit ~21 K above published (720.7/272.9 degC vs 700/250). REPORTED, NOT TUNED OUT.

Suite: 285 lib / 19 fhr_sim_v2 / 53 htgr_sim_v1 / 21 widget_studio, 0 failed. Example launches and runs clean.
title: htgr_sim_v1: nodalised implicit counter-flow steam generator (helium/metal/water)
